23796.question_text: A boy measured the length and breath of a rectangular lawn as 59.6m and 40.3m respectively instead of 60m and 40m. What is the percentage error in his calculation of the perimeter of the lawn?
23796.explanation:
Length = 59.6m
Breath = 40.3m
Perimeter = (59.6m + 40.3m) x 2
= 99.9 x 2 = 199.8m
Actual measurement
Perimeter = (60 + 40) x 2 = 100 x 2 = 200m
Error = 200m - 199.8m = 0.2

Error =0.2/200 x 100/1

= 0.1%

23804.subject: Mathematics
23804.question_text: Make p the subject if formula y = \(\frac{a + p}{a - p}\)
23804.explanation:
To make \( p \) the subject of the formula \( y = \frac{a + p}{a - p} \):

Start with the equation:
\(y = \frac{a + p}{a - p}\)

Cross-multiply: \(y(a - p) = a + p\)

Distribute \( y \): \(ya - yp = a + p\)

Rearrange to isolate terms involving \( p \): \(ya - a = p + yp\)

Factor out \( p \) on the right side: \(ya - a = p(1 + y)\)

Finally, solve for \( p \): \(p = \frac{ya - a}{1 + y}\)

Thus, the formula with \( p \) as the subject is: \(p = \frac{a(y - 1)}{y + 1}\)

23837.subject: Mathematics
23837.question_text: What percentage of observation lie outside interquartile range of any distribution?
23837.explanation:
Q1 represents the value below which 25% of the data falls, while Q3 indicates the value below which 75% of the data falls (or above which 25% falls). Consequently, the percentage of data outside the interval [Q1, Q3] is 50%, composed of 25% on each side.

This principle applies to any distribution, as quartiles are determined by order statistics and cumulative probabilities, independent of the distribution's shape
